method: For each eval_week replay book independently: begin at that week's realized start equity; at each unique exit timestamp realize all exits due at that timestamp as one accounting batch; mark-to-market only positions from that same replay book still open after the batch; calculate peak-to-trough equity drawdown inside that book; report the worst drawdown across the 26 books.
why_legacy_global_event_dd_is_not_author: The 26-week research runner replays each evaluated week as a separate portfolio book. Positions in one book may have exit timestamps beyond the calendar boundary while the next week's book is replayed separately. Globally sorting event-equity rows therefore interleaves accounting states from different replay books. Same-timestamp exits were also serialized, allowing transient marks before the full exit batch was accounted.

original_34.interpretation: Authoritative event DD is numerically consistent with the exact weekly-book drawdown once same-book mark-to-market accounting is reconstructed.

exact_50.interpretation: The prior -5.2468% headline was a cross-book/same-timestamp reporting artifact; the corrected event DD does not change any trade or P&L.

corrected_conclusion: On an apples-to-apples batch-consistent basis, the exact 50 improved event drawdown versus the 34 control while also increasing ending equity and trade throughput. Fresh independent validation remains required before production-universe promotion.
